jobId.description: Becomes a directory name under `project-data/jobs/`. The pattern is defence in depth — `jobDir()` in @cutdown/skill-runtime guards and containment-checks it regardless of caller, because a skill's `entrypoint` is a documented direct invocation.

assetId.description: The ingested SourceAsset to index. Indexing is per-asset: a multi-asset job indexes each asset separately so one unindexable asset cannot cost the whole job its work.

speakerMapPath.description: Optional YAML mapping stable speaker-turn IDs to corrected names (REQ-011). An unknown turn ID or a duplicate correction is a validation failure; the original inference is preserved alongside the correction either way.

noVlm.description: Skip the visual-description sub-stage. Defaults to TRUE — the fail-closed choice while the decisions.md D-21 spend ceiling is unset, since the alternative default would spend a client's money without a ceiling in place. A skipped sub-stage records status `skipped` with a reason and produces no descriptions; it never fabricates one.

force.description: Sub-stages to re-run even when a valid checkpoint exists. Named rather than a blanket boolean so re-running OCR does not discard an expensive transcript.

skip.description: Sub-stages to skip by operator request. Only `ocr` is skippable: it is the one stage nothing downstream requires (captions and retrieval are transcript-driven; Moment entities lose their ocr-source entries), and on real footage it is ~90% of indexing cost. The ledger records the skip with its reason — a skipped stage never reads as 'looked and found nothing'. An explicit skip WINS over an explicit force of the same stage (the --no-vlm-beats---vlm precedent).

ocrThreads.description: CPU threads for the PaddleOCR engine. The shipped default (1) buys byte-identical re-runs — thread count changes float reduction order, so >1 trades that reproducibility for roughly 2× wall-clock (measured: 31 s/frame at 1 thread, 17 s at 8). The value enters the engine config and therefore the REQ-005 cache key: changing it re-indexes rather than serving a checkpoint produced under different ordering.
